title: Marche's LPG Price Jumps 7% Overnight While Methane Keeps Climbing Toward a Four-Month High
dek: A sudden single-day GPL spike breaks eleven weeks of flat pricing in the region, even as natural gas extends its steady summer-to-fall climb both locally and nationwide.
executive_summary: Today, Marche's self-service Benzina sits at €2.0062/L, essentially flat day-over-day (-€0.0018, -0.09%) and 0.34% below the national average of €2.0130. Gasolio is €2.2384/L (-€0.0010 day-over-day, -0.04%), also running 0.48% under the €2.2493 national mark. GPL is today's outlier: it jumped to €0.959/L, up 6.67% (+€0.060) from yesterday's €0.899 — a price that had sat virtually unchanged since August 20 — and now trades 17.9% above the national GPL average of €0.8132. Metano continues its steady ascent, reaching €2.1083/L (+1.22% day-over-day), landing almost exactly level with the national average of €2.1058.

Zoom out across the 16 weeks tracked since July 21, and Metano is by far the biggest mover for both Marche and Italy as a whole — up 41.6% regionally and 38.1% nationally, with the pace actually accelerating in the most recent week (Marche +8.0%, national +10.2% week-over-week). Gasolio and Benzina have each climbed a more modest 2-4% over the full period, both peaking in late September before cooling off. GPL is the real divergence story: nationally it has been grinding higher in a straight line (+5.3% since July), while in Marche it sat dead flat at €0.899 for eleven straight weeks before today's abrupt 6.7% jump — a move sharp enough, and sudden enough, to be worth watching again tomorrow.

fuel_sections.heading: Petrol Holds Steady, Trading Below the National Average
paragraphs: Marche's self-service Benzina price is €2.0062/L today, down a negligible €0.0018 (-0.09%) from yesterday's €2.008. That keeps the region 0.34% cheaper than the national self-service average of €2.0130/L, continuing a pattern of Marche pricing petrol slightly under the Italy-wide figure.

Over the 16 tracked weeks, Marche's weekly average Benzina price rose from €1.9544 (week of July 20) to €2.0096 (week of November 2), a 2.82% increase — marginally outpacing the national rise of 2.11% over the same span (€1.9756 to €2.0173). Both series peaked in the week of September 21 before easing back; in the most recent tracked week, Marche's average fell 1.10% while the national average fell a steeper 1.39%, suggesting the broader market is cooling slightly faster than Marche right now.

fuel_sections.heading: Diesel Cools From Its Late-September Peak, Still Pricier Than a Month Ago
paragraphs: Marche's self-service Gasolio sits at €2.2384/L today, down €0.0010 (-0.04%) day-over-day, and 0.48% below the €2.2493 national self-service average.

The multi-week picture shows Marche diesel climbing faster than the national average through the summer and into autumn: from €2.1524 (week of July 20) to €2.2438 (week of November 2), a 4.25% rise, versus 3.72% nationally (€2.1747 to €2.2556). Both series peaked in the week of September 21 — Marche at €2.3496, national at €2.3736 — and have since pulled back, with Marche down 4.50% from that peak and the national average down 4.97%, a slightly deeper correction nationally than regionally.

fuel_sections.heading: A Sudden 7% Jump Breaks Eleven Weeks of Flat LPG Pricing
paragraphs: Marche's self-service GPL price jumped to €0.959/L today, up €0.060 (+6.67%) from yesterday's €0.899 — the first move of any size since the price settled at €0.899 back on August 20. That one-day jump pushes Marche's GPL price 17.9% above today's national self-service average of €0.8132/L.

Zoomed out, the weekly-average trend tells a quieter story than today's spike suggests: Marche's GPL rose just 2.47% over the full 16 weeks (€0.889 to €0.911), while the national average climbed more steadily and faster, up 5.30% (€0.7592 to €0.7994) over the same stretch. In other words, Marche had been the calmer of the two all season — until today's abrupt jump, which on its own is larger than the region's entire prior four-month drift and is worth confirming holds in tomorrow's data rather than reversing as a one-day anomaly.

fuel_sections.heading: Natural Gas Extends Its Climb Toward the Steepest Rise of the Season
paragraphs: Marche's self-service Metano price reached €2.1083/L today, up €0.0255 (+1.22%) from yesterday's €2.0828, landing just €0.0025 (+0.12%) above today's national self-service average of €2.1058/L — essentially in line with the rest of the country.

Metano is the standout mover of the four fuels tracked: Marche's weekly average rose 41.63% from €1.4581 (week of July 20) to €2.0647 (week of November 2), slightly ahead of the national rise of 38.08% (€1.4999 to €2.071) over the same period. The climb is not slowing down — in the most recent tracked week alone, Marche's average rose 8.01% and the national average rose 10.18%, meaning the national price is now closing the gap with Marche's by rising even faster week-on-week.

network_section.heading: 724 of 779 Marche Stations Reporting Today — Slightly Ahead of the National Rate
paragraphs: Marche has 779 registered fuel stations in today's data, of which 724 reported prices — a 92.9% reporting rate. That compares to 21,655 of 23,951 stations reporting nationally, a 90.4% rate, putting Marche a touch ahead of the national average for data completeness today.

A reporting rate in the low-to-mid 90s is typical for this pipeline and reflects normal day-to-day gaps in MIMIT's self-reported price feed rather than station closures — the registered count for Marche has actually crept up slightly over the tracked period, from 774 stations on July 21 to 779 today, suggesting the regional network is marginally expanding even as a handful of stations skip reporting on any given day.

methodology_section.heading: Built by an Unattended Pipeline, Not a Spreadsheet
paragraphs: Everything in this report — the daily price pull from MIMIT's feed, the region-of-the-day rotation, the weekly trend calculations comparing Marche to the national average, and the prose you just read — is produced automatically every morning by an unattended pipeline built with Claude Code. No analyst opens a spreadsheet, recalculates a weekly average, or drafts a paragraph; the pipeline reads the raw station-level data, computes the comparisons, and writes the report from the numbers it finds, start to finish.

That is a deliberate contrast with how a project like this is usually run: a person manually downloading a CSV, pasting it into a tracking spreadsheet, and writing up a summary by hand — a process that is slow, easy to let slip on a busy day, and hard to extend to new fuels, regions, or comparisons. Fuel Dashboard instead treats the report as code: the same logic runs every day, for whichever region comes up next in the rotation, with no manual step in between the raw data and the published page.

pull_quote: Marche's LPG price just jumped 6.7% in a single day — after sitting frozen at €0.899 for eleven straight weeks.
caption:
Today's Fuel Dashboard spotlight: Marche. The headline isn't petrol or diesel — it's GPL, which jumped 6.7% overnight (€0.899 to €0.959/L) after sitting completely flat for eleven straight weeks, while Metano keeps climbing toward its steepest rise of the season, up over 40% regionally since late July.
